claims.head: A shadow job for Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg
claims.call: The Lightning’s L2 (Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg) spends at least 56% of its 5-on-5 time against the Oilers’ first line, against about 45% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Mikheyev’s line (Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Oilers’ first line is Podkolzin, McDavid and Draisaitl.

notes.text: Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 51% of the team’s power-play time in 20 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, down from 30% last season.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 6 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Conor Geekie takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Emil Lilleberg is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside McDonagh and Crozier.
Anthony Cirelli is day to day (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. Nikita Kucherov has taken his spot beside Jake Guentzel and Brandon Hagel.

story.head: A heavyweight meeting
paras: The Lightning have won two in a row, and the Oilers have won three straight. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Bolts first in the Atlantic (tied for fifth).

The Oilers’ record (.775) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.574), largely thanks to their finishing. So is the Lightning’s (.737 on chances worth .669), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Oilers (2nd) and the Lightning (4th) both rarely ice the puck. The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest) and have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd). Edmonton has scored 4.00 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Lightning, they keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), but don't block many shots (29th). Tampa Bay has scored 3.89 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Lightning shoot a lot, but the Oilers don’t.

Connor McDavid (11 G / 38 A / 49 P in 20 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with ten points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (18 G / 19 A / 37 P in 20 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, the most in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Nikita Kucherov (8 G / 20 A / 28 P in 19 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Edmonton. Brandon Hagel (13 G / 11 A / 24 P in 19 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, sixth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games.
Tristan Jarry (5-1-3 / .903 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Edmonton, and Andrei Vasilevskiy (9-4-1 / .884 SV% in 14 GS) for Tampa Bay.

At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Podkolzin, McDavid and Draisaitl. Elsewhere, the Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Oilers do.
